title: Enabling multi-resolution droplet-on-demand metal jetting through tailored pulsing

published_experiment.apparatus: Modified Xerox ElemX; two-orifice graphite lower nozzle, boron-nitride upper nozzle

mechanism: Approximately triangular coil-current pulses induce circulating liquid current. Radial force during the rising/falling portions provides a push/pull pressure history.
application_to_this_study: Supports testing a single shaped pulse instead of relying on the earlier AC-burst screen. Does not demonstrate our stainless chamber, solder alloys,250A limit or24/48V supply. Different geometry, winding, conductivity and fluid inertia prevent transferring the published current as our required current.
uncertainty: The paper's reported circuit drive voltage is not silently reinterpreted as a supply or every switch-node maximum. Published drive time is not assumed to equal our complete rise-plus-fall duration. No equivalent winding turn-count, ampere-turn or inductance comparison is asserted.
